主要内容: In 2018, U.S. housing prices were rising faster than the rate of inflation, with some areas seeing increases three times higher. This trend was observed in both high-cost cities like Seattle and San Francisco, as well as lower-cost cities such as Charlotte and Tampa. The rapid increase in home prices was causing significant strain on the middle class, making it increasingly difficult for them to achieve the American dream of homeownership. Nationally, home prices were approaching the peak levels seen in 2006, just before the housing market collapsed into a foreclosure crisis and the economy plunged into the Great Recession. Major cities across the country, including Los Angeles, Washington, D.C., Cleveland, and Chicago, were all experiencing rising home prices, with some reaching or nearing historical highs.
